description: Issues for the GitHub automations approved on 2026-10-23, one per pull request, in a new Project tooling milestone. Applied by the Maintenance workflow (apply-issue-updates).

milestones.Project tooling: GitHub automations and project docs: checks, weekly update, Maintenance buttons, contributor docs. Not app features.

A1.title: Weekly update issue every Friday
A1.what: Every Friday at 4:00 PM Chicago time (staying at 4:00 PM across daylight saving), post an issue labeled "weekly" listing pull requests merged and issues opened or closed since the previous Friday 4:01 PM, using each pull request's own plain-words description. No AI writes it. The same script is a Maintenance button for any date range.
done: Scheduled run posts on Fridays at 4:00 PM America/Chicago, in both daylight and standard time
Maintenance weekly-update button works for any date range, with dry run on by default
Tested with dry runs before merge

A2.title: Pull request rule checker
A2.what: On every pull request, check the AGENTS.md rules with actions/github-script: flag more than about 400 changed lines (lock files aside), a missing issue link, missing Tested / Not tested sections or a missing "Based on" line, and remove "Generated by Claude Code" footers.
done: Missing issue link, Tested, Not tested or Based on gives a red X; size over about 400 lines warns
Footers and session links are removed from the description automatically
One comment per pull request, updated in place
Tested on a throwaway pull request

A3.title: License check for new dependencies
A3.what: Check every pull request's new dependencies with actions/dependency-review-action against the allowed licenses: MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC; MPL-2.0 only as an unmodified dependency.
done: A pull request adding a dependency with a license outside the list fails the check
Tested with a pull request that adds a disallowed dependency

A4.title: Dependabot updates for npm, Cargo and GitHub Actions
A4.what: Add a Dependabot configuration so GitHub opens pull requests when npm packages, Rust crates or GitHub Actions have updates.
done: dependabot.yml covers npm, Cargo (src-tauri) and GitHub Actions
GitHub shows the configuration as valid

A5.title: Maintenance buttons: issue health, screenshot cleanup, Mac test
A5.what: Add three Maintenance buttons: an issue health report (issues with no milestone, pull requests open more than a few days, tasks whose sub-issues are all closed but which are still open), screenshot cleanup (delete screenshots of merged pull requests from the ci-screenshots branch), and a Mac test (cargo test on a GitHub Mac; never a required check).
done: Each button runs from Actions -> Maintenance and has a dry run where it changes anything
The Mac test is not a required check
Each button tested on GitHub

A6.title: Docs for people: PR template, CONTRIBUTING, roadmap pointer
A6.what: Add a pull request template with a "Based on" line (the existing library, official doc or known pattern the change follows, or "new code, because nothing fit: ..."), a short CONTRIBUTING.md for people (AGENTS.md stays the agent rules), a "Where we are" line in the README pointing to the roadmap and milestones, and the matching rule in AGENTS.md.
done: New pull requests open with the template
CONTRIBUTING.md and the README line exist; AGENTS.md has the Based on rule
The PR rule checker passes on a pull request made from the template

A7.title: Agent handoff: who works on what
A7.what: Let Blake hand sets of issues to different agents (Claude, Codex, others) and see at a glance what is free, assigned, in progress, in review or paused, using labels and pull requests that every agent can read and change (the Roadmap board's Status field needs GraphQL, which agents cannot use). Labels: `ready` (free to pick up), `agent:claude` / `agent:codex` (assigned by Blake), `paused` (with a comment saying why; `needs decision` works the same way). In progress = a draft pull request with "Closes #N"; in review = that pull request marked ready. Blake's direct instruction always overrides the labels: an agent told to take an issue labeled for another agent takes it and moves the label to itself.
done: The labels exist with short descriptions

AGENTS.md says: take only issues labeled `ready` plus your agent label with no linked open pull request, unless Blake says otherwise; open a draft pull request with "Closes #N" first; move the label when told to take another agent's issue
The issue health report flags stale claims (a draft pull request with no activity for a few days)
Tested by labeling an issue for one agent and having another agent take it on Blake's instruction
